rationale: C13 plausibly supplied a material administrative template: a Commerce-chaired cabinet-level trade committee composed largely of the same departments, responsible for policy issues and positioned above an interdepartmental committee carrying out the program. The child adapts that layered machinery to textiles by placing a Commerce-chaired interagency administrative committee beneath a Cabinet Textile Advisory Committee, with policy questions escalated to the cabinet committee. C09 reinforces the policy-referral mechanism but has less similar membership and no comparable two-tier committee structure. C04 parallels the allocation of foreign negotiations to State with substantive participation by other agencies, but is less concrete as a drafting model for the child's full arrangement.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Interagency Textile Administrative Committee is to be established under the Chairmanship of a designee of the Secretary of Commerce; ... composed of ... representatives ... from the Departments of State, Treasury, Agriculture, and Labor.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: There is hereby established the Trade Policy Committee, consisting of the Secretary of State, the Secretary of the Treasury, ... the Secretary of Agriculture, the Secretary of Commerce, and the Secretary of Labor ... The Secretary of Commerce or his alternate shall be the Chairman
shared_material.explanation: The child closely adapts C13's Commerce-chaired interagency trade body and much of its departmental membership.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The President's Cabinet Textile Advisory Committee will ... consider any question of policy relating to the administration of the "Short-Term Arrangement."
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Trade Policy Committee shall make recommendations to the President on basic policy issues arising in the administration of the trade-agreements program, which ... shall guide the Interdepartmental Committee on Trade Agreements ... in carrying out its functions.
shared_material.explanation: Both use a higher-level policy committee to guide a subordinate interdepartmental body administering a trade program.
